# Lintel v4.0 — The Reframe (master design doc, v2.0)

**Generated by:** `/office-hours` on 2026-05-29 · revised post-`/plan-eng-review` on same day
**Status:** **READY_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION** — 23 review findings (PR #34) absorbed inline; full scope preserved per operator decision
**Mode:** Builder (engineering scaffolding for the next generation of Lintel)
**Supersedes:** v1.0 of this doc (PR #33). Extends v3.5 doc-gen, v3.6 cohort backlog, v3.7 frontend family, v3.8 jobs + planner-module.

> Five inputs landed on the desk in one session: two design docs, one text request about engineering depth, and a meta-process note about infrastructure-for-infrastructure. They are not five separate features. They are **one coherent reframe** — what Lintel **is**, what every workflow inside it **must guarantee**, how depth gets specced for the engineering domains we actually live in, and how Lintel evolves itself without breaking what already runs.
>
> v2.0 retains full scope (operator-locked) while resolving every finding from `/plan-eng-review` (PR #34). The L-001 + L-002 disciplines that the review surfaced are now load-bearing in the module pattern; the puddle path is explicitly rejected and the lake-path is the scope.

# §1 Architectural intent · portability from day one

## 1.1 Why this reframe at all

Three observations from re-reading v3.5 through v3.8:

**A. Lintel already does most of v4.0 informally.** BUILD scene-sets implementer subagents with task + criteria + companion skills. Cycle propagates state between phases. Hooks fire at the right moments. Lessons compound. v4.0 makes the informal mechanical. The risk of a re-write disguised as a refactor is real; the antidote is the meta-infra discipline in Chapter 4 — which governs even this reframe's own implementation.

**B. v4.0 is consolidation, not invention.** Every previous milestone — the cohort sequencing, the frontend family separation, the jobs system, the planner-as-module — was a step toward this. The doc your're reading captures what the architecture has been pointing toward since v3.6.

**C. Operator's bold-and-responsible stance is the design constraint, not a style.** Every gate ships with override + audit. Every novice protection that would slow the operator is refused. Pack policies are configured once and apply mechanically. The system trusts the operator to use overrides responsibly.

## 1.2 The four lessons made architectural

The lesson-quartet from v3.x already shapes v4.0; the doc surfaces this so future readers understand the rationale:

| Lesson | Architectural consequence in v4.0 |
|---|---|
| **L-001** scaffolding-not-content | Packs ship content. Spine ships scaffolding. Engineering-module sub-skills ship **workflow + dispatch contracts**, not curated answers. The whole reframe is L-001 made structural. |
| **L-002** grep-first | Spine extraction (Ch.1 FR-A) is L-002 applied at "what's hardcoded that shouldn't be." Per-module L-002 inventory is mandatory pre-PR (Ch.3). Every module declares what it REUSES from existing skills/agents before declaring what it adds. |
| **L-003** verify-counts | Every count in this doc has been or will be verified via `find` / `wc` before code starts. CLAUDE.md count-strings get auto-regenerated by the wiki-gen (Ch.2.C scope). |
| **L-004** separate decisions from execution | Spine = execution-engine. Packs = decision-layer. Engineering-module `full` granularity = decision (which pattern to apply). `single` granularity = execution (run the chosen sub-skill). Two clean L-004 splits at different scales. |

## 1.3 Portability axis — load-bearing from day one

Portability is woven through every chapter, not deferred to an appendix. Four dimensions:

### 1.3.1 Multi-CLI portability

Lintel ships as a plugin to ten agentic coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI, Factory Droid, Gemini CLI; OpenCode/Cline/Continue/Aider planned). Every skill MUST declare `cli_support` in frontmatter with a per-CLI degradation strategy.

v4.0 enforces:
- `cli_support:` frontmatter mandatory at load (frontmatter-lint extended)
- Plugin manifest auto-generated from skill set per CLI (eliminates per-CLI shim drift)
- `instruction-parity-check` runs in CI on every PR (closes v3.6 gap)

### 1.3.2 Pack portability

Operator can take a pack across machines. v4.0 mandates:
- All identity-bound state flows through `PackResolver` (§2.4)
- Pack export/import (Ch.1 FR-B.7/B.8) bundles deterministically
- Pack inheritance (`extends:`) is shallow-merged with documented precedence
- `share_excludes` mechanic prevents customer-data leakage on export

### 1.3.3 Schema portability

Every contract JSON declares `schema_version`. v4.0 mandates:
- Envelope (Ch.2.B), pack manifest (Ch.1.B), frontend-design-spec (v3.7), evaluator results (Ch.2.A) — all version-bearing
- Schema-migration helpers ship in `lib/schema-migrations/`
- `bin/li-schema-validate` runs at load + in CI

### 1.3.4 Audit + provenance portability

Audit logs are append-only JSONL — grep-portable, git-portable, time-orderable, replay-able:
- `~/.lintel/audit/jobs.jsonl` (v3.8)
- `~/.lintel/audit/alias-resolution.jsonl` (v3.6)
- `~/.lintel/audit/hooks.jsonl` (v3.6)
- `~/.lintel/audit/brief-forge.jsonl` (v4.0 Ch.2)
- `~/.lintel/audit/meta-infra-overrides.jsonl` (v4.0 Ch.4, per finding 1-P2.2 resolution)
- `~/.lintel/audit/envelopes/<job-id>/` (v4.0 Ch.2)

All shippable to backup, queryable by jq, replay-able via `bin/li-envelope-replay --dry-run` (Ch.2.B).

## 1.4 Composition view — how the chapters interlock

```
Operator types something
       ↓
SPINE reads PACK via PackResolver (Ch.1)
       ↓
NAVIGATION orientator at SENSE reads request + pack + open jobs (Ch.1)
       ↓
→ picks workflow + entry-phase + risk-level
       ↓
workflow_root spawns job (v3.8)
       ↓
At each hand-off → BRIEF FORGE evaluates → produces ENVELOPE (Ch.2)
       ↓
Within BUILD, ENGINEERING DOMAIN MODULES may activate (Ch.3)
       ↓
If work is harness-on-harness → META-INFRA mode + 4 mandatory gates (Ch.4)
       ↓
CAPTURE writes envelopes + lessons + ADRs
       ↓
WIKI regenerates from all of the above (Ch.2.C)
```

**Closing thought:** v4.0 is not a feature push. It is the discipline of v3.x made mechanical, with portability as an axis rather than an afterthought.

# §2 Chapter 1 — Generic spine + packs + navigation

## 2.1 Why this chapter goes first

Without spine extraction (FR-A), every other chapter depends on something contaminated by CAIP-SE assumptions. Without packs (FR-B), the spine has nothing to read at session-start. Without navigation (FR-C), workflow_root declarations are advisory. Without CAIP-SE lifted into pack format (FR-D), operator's own daily workflow breaks during transition.

**Ship order within Chapter 1: A → B → D → C** (D before C lets orientator test against a real pack).

## 2.2 FR-A — Generic spine extraction

Operator's spec stands. Three additions in v2.0:

**A.7 — Pack-resolver test harness, with expanded matrix.** Per finding 3-P2.2, ship `tests/unit/pack-resolver-fallbacks.sh` covering at least these 9 scenarios:

1. No pack active → all resolver calls return `_default` value
2. Mock pack active → resolver returns pack value
3. Malformed pack.yaml → resolver hard-fails SENSE with operator-readable error
4. `extends:` cycle → resolver detects + refuses to activate
5. Missing required field → pack-validation hook rejects at load
6. Two skills resolving same key concurrently → both get identical (cached) value
7. Pack-switch mid-cycle → cached value for the current cycle remains; next cycle picks up new
8. Pack file deleted after SENSE read → cached value remains valid for cycle lifetime
9. Resolver internal bug → fallback to `_default` + warn to stderr + audit-log

**A.8 — Audit deliverable as PR artifact.** A.1 (audit core skills for pack-specific assumptions) produces a list. Ships as `docs/v4.x/structure-changes/2026-XX-spine-extraction-audit.md` (per finding 2-P1.1 path-unification). Cited grep commands must be reproducible per L-003.

**A.9 — Path-naming convention.** All meta-infra outputs use `docs/v4.x/<artifact-class>/<date>-<slug>.md`. Classes: `structure-changes` · `migrations` · `compatibility-audits` · `shape-test-reports`. No `docs/v4.0/` (point release) anywhere. Closes finding 2-P1.1.

## 2.3 FR-B — Pack architecture and lifecycle

Operator's pack schema, lifecycle skills, inheritance, validation hook — all sound. Three decision-locks:

| Decision | Recommendation | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| C1-D1 `ms-internal` base pack | **NOW** | ~1h cost. Pays dividends the moment any sister-pack to CAIP-SE shows up. |
| C1-D2 Pack-version block-vs-warn | **warn-only for v4.0; block from v4.1** | Pack ecosystem doesn't exist yet. Block in v4.0 is theater. |
| C1-D3 Default `auto_mode_eligible` | **false** | Conservative for new mechanism. Operator opts in per workflow. |

**Pack manifest extension for Brief Forge (per Ch.2):** `pack.yaml` includes a `brief_forge_handoffs:` block. Schema in §2.5.4.

**Pack manifest extension for navigation (per FR-C):** `pack.yaml` includes a `navigation:` block with `orientator_budget_tokens` (default 2000, pack-overridable) + `orientator_max_output_tokens` (default 200) + `escalation_threshold` (`never|low|medium|high`, default `medium`). Closes findings 1-P2.3 + 4-P2.3.

## 2.4 Pack-resolver failure semantics (§1.2.1 — new in v2.0, resolves 1-P1.1)

PackResolver is the critical-path interface used by ~30+ skills. Failure modes are explicit:

| Failure | Behavior | Audit |
|---|---|---|
| Pack.yaml parse error | Hard-fail SENSE with operator-readable error citing line:col | `audit/pack-resolver.jsonl` |
| `extends:` cycle detected | Refuse activation; surface chain; revert to previous active pack | yes |
| Missing required field | Pack-validation hook rejects at load; previous pack stays active | yes |
| Resolver internal bug | Fallback to `_default` pack values; warn to stderr | yes |
| Pack-switch mid-cycle | Current cycle continues with cached values; next cycle picks new | yes |
| Pack file deleted post-SENSE | Cached values valid for cycle lifetime; warn on next SENSE | yes |

**Caching contract (closes 4-P2.2):** PackResolver parses `pack.yaml` once at SENSE Step 1. Parsed structure is cached for the cycle's lifetime. All resolver calls during the cycle hit the cache. New cycle invocation = re-parse. This makes pack-value access deterministic for jobs + replay.

**Neutral defaults skeleton (closes 1-P3.1):** `packs/_default/pack.yaml` ships as part of FR-A.4. Every field documented with neutral value:

```yaml
name: _default
version: 1.0.0
shareable: false

voice:
  default_tier: internal
  corpus: null
  enforce: none

compliance:
  mode: advisory
  hooks: []
  workprofile_default: off

persona:
  source: null
  voice_alignment: false

roles:
  source: null
  default_role: null

brand:
  templates: null
  color_tokens: null

knowhow:
  source: null
  override_session_priors: false

lessons:
  packaged: null
  operator_lessons: ~/.lintel/lessons.md

opinions:
  source: null

navigation:
  default_workflow: cycle
  high_risk_workflows: [cycle, plan, ship]
  orientator_budget_tokens: 2000
  orientator_max_output_tokens: 200
  escalation_threshold: medium

brief_forge_handoffs:
  on_subagent_spawn:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [security, stale]
  on_phase_transition:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [completeness]
  on_workflow_handoff:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [completeness]
  on_cold_executor:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [security, completeness]
  on_operator_input:
    enabled: false
    evaluators: []
  cold_path_bypass:
    eligible_skills: []  # skills can declare brief_forge_handoffs: skip in their frontmatter
  budget_tokens: 5000
  override_allowed: true
  override_requires_audit: true
```

## 2.5 FR-C — Navigation as architectural guarantee

**Mandatory `navigation:` block on every `workflow_root: true` skill.** Spine rejects skills missing the block at load.

```yaml
# Every workflow_root: true skill MUST declare
workflow_root: true

navigation:
  valid_entries: [<phase>, <phase>, ...]
  valid_exits: [<phase>, <phase>, ...]
  auto_mode_eligible: false   # default per C1-D3
  risk_level: low | medium | high
  brief_forge_handoffs:        # canonical field name per finding 2-P2.2
    on_subagent_spawn: [...]   # which evaluators per handoff-type, OR `skip`
    on_phase_transition: [...]
    on_workflow_handoff: [...]
    on_cold_executor: [...]
```

Empty `brief_forge_handoffs.<type>` = inherits from pack's pack.yaml policy. Explicit `skip` = cold-path bypass (closes 1-P2.1).

### 2.5.1 Orientator agent at SENSE

Reads operator request + active pack + open jobs. Routes mechanically; escalates to LLM only when needed.

**Mechanical-first routing (closes 1-P2.3 + 4-P2.3):**

1. Parse request: extract intent verbs (fix/build/research/review/ship/scaffold/audit), file paths, job IDs, service names. Cost: near zero.
2. Job lookup: scan `_active.md` for tag intersection with request. Cost: trivial.
3. Pack-route: map intent + pack's `default_workflow` + tag match → workflow + entry-phase. Cost: trivial.
4. **LLM escalation triggers** (mechanical-first; LLM only if ALL these match):
   - Mechanical routing has ambiguity score > 0.3 across top-2 candidate workflows, AND
   - Operator request matches zero pack-declared entry-phases, AND
   - Active escalation_threshold ≤ `medium`
5. LLM is called with: input cap 2000 tokens (pack-configurable), output cap 200 tokens (200-byte JSON object).

### 2.5.2 Auto-mode level (b)

| Risk level | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `low` + `auto_mode_eligible: true` | Auto-start. Log to audit. Operator interrupts if wrong. |
| `medium` or `high` | Confirm with operator: "Auto-mode wants: `<workflow>` from `<phase>`, est ~`<N>k` tokens. Run / change / cancel?" |
| Pack has no `default_workflow` and no clear match | Fall back to ask |

Operator override always wins:
- `--no-auto` flag kills orientator
- `~/.lintel/config.yaml` `auto_mode: off` disables globally
- Override audit-logged to `~/.lintel/audit/meta-infra-overrides.jsonl` (note: this is the unified audit store per finding 1-P2.2; orientator overrides + meta-infra overrides land in the same log keyed by `category` field)

## 2.6 FR-D — CAIP-SE as reference pack

Migrate existing CAIP-SE-specific content (Trailblazer corpus, MS hooks, personas, roles, brand templates) into `packs/caip-se/`. Activate as operator's default. Document as canonical pack-building example.

**Migration mechanic:** `git mv`-heavy. Per finding ms-internal-base-now decision (C1-D1 = NOW), the chain is:

```
packs/
├── _default/         ← neutral, ships in repo, copied on install
├── ms-internal/      ← MS-policy baseline (extends _default)
├── caip-se/          ← extends ms-internal (CAIP-SE specific)
└── <operator-custom>/  ← extends caip-se OR ms-internal OR _default
```

## 2.7 Chapter 1 closing thought

Spine = execution engine. Packs = identity. Navigation = the binding that makes the engine route correctly. **The 9-scenario test harness + pack-resolver failure semantics + neutral defaults skeleton make pack-resolver bulletproof from day one.** Closes the singleton bus-factor concern.

# §3 Chapter 2 — Brief Forge + envelope + generated wiki

## 3.1 The architectural purpose

Chapter 1 gives the spine an identity and a router. Chapter 2 gives it a **contract at every boundary crossing**. Without Brief Forge, the new spine+packs system can still pass uncurated payloads between phases — meaning all the work in Chapter 1 produces a flexible engine that still has hand-off-quality drift.

Brief Forge isn't a feature on top of v3.8. **It's the layer that finally lets v4.0's mechanical engine produce mechanical quality.**

## 3.2 FR-A — Brief Forge: the universal hand-off gate

Three-phase mechanic at every hand-off (operator → skill, skill → subagent, phase → phase, workflow → sub-workflow, workflow → cold executor).

### 3.2.1 The three phases

**Curate (sender's responsibility):**
- *What I believe the situation is* (one-paragraph summary)
- *What I'm asking the receiver to do* (task, verbatim)
- *What the receiver needs that may not be obvious* (anticipated context)
- *What I'm NOT including and why* (deliberate exclusions)

**Hydrate (gate's responsibility, policy-driven):**
- Knowledge-base lookup (tag-match against active pack's knowhow)
- Lessons surface (tag-match against `tasks/lessons.md`)
- Context-warming (synthetic always; real on completeness fail)
- Stale-check (timestamps vs threshold)
- Dependency completeness (declared `consumes` present?)

**Dispatch (gate's responsibility):**
- Direct pass if policy says so
- Policy-matched evaluators in parallel where possible
- Block-with-override if any evaluator returns hard-fail

### 3.2.2 Evaluator registry (resolves 2-A.1)

Built-in and pack-defined evaluators discovered through a single registry:

```
lib/brief-forge/evaluators/
├── _registry.yaml             ← built-in evaluator declarations
├── security-eval.sh
├── compliance-eval.sh
├── voice-eval.sh
├── stale-eval.sh
├── completeness-eval.sh
├── knowledge-overlap-eval.sh
└── legality-eval.sh

packs/<pack>/brief-forge/evaluators/
└── <pack-defined>-eval.sh    ← pack-specific; auto-discovered at pack-load
```

**Naming convention (closes 2-P2.3):**
- Evaluator ID: kebab-case-no-suffix (`security`, `voice`, `knowledge-overlap`)
- Filename: `<id>-eval.sh`
- References in pack.yaml + frontmatter use the ID only

### 3.2.3 Per-handoff-type policy with enabled flag (resolves A.2)

```yaml
brief_forge_handoffs:
  on_subagent_spawn:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [security, completeness]
  on_phase_transition:
    enabled: false           # pack-decision: this handoff-type doesn't gate
    evaluators: []
  on_cold_executor:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [security, compliance, completeness, voice]
```

`enabled: true` by default if `evaluators:` non-empty.

### 3.2.4 Cold-path bypass (resolves 1-P2.1)

Trivial skills (read-only, no subagent spawn, no phase transition) can declare `brief_forge_handoffs: skip` in their own frontmatter. The pack policy is then bypassed for that skill.

**Eligibility criteria for `skip`:**
- Skill has `tools:` containing only `Read | Grep | Glob` (no Write/Edit/Bash/Agent)
- Skill is not `workflow_root: true`
- Skill is not invoked from inside another workflow_root job

Validated at load. Frontmatter-lint extended to enforce eligibility.

### 3.2.5 Performance contract

- Budget: 5000 tokens TOTAL across all evaluators per hand-off (pack-overridable)
- Mechanical-first: regex + tag-match + timestamp + dependency-check all run before any LLM
- Parallel execution: independent evaluators run concurrently
- Telemetry: per-evaluator `{pass|fail|duration_ms}` triple written to envelope TAIL
- Measurement protocol (closes 3-P2.3): p95 wall-clock latency over 100 invocations with all default-pack evaluators enabled, mechanical-only path, cold-cache, measured via `lib/brief-forge/bench.sh`. Target: p95 < 1000ms.

### 3.2.6 Override-with-audit

`--no-brief-forge` flag OR `BRIEF_FORGE_OVERRIDE=1` env var. Logged to `~/.lintel/audit/brief-forge.jsonl`:

```json
{"ts":"...","kind":"override","handoff_type":"...","reason":"...","operator":"...","cycle_id":"..."}
```

Per the bold-operator stance: gate refuses, operator can force, audit captures.

## 3.3 FR-B — Standardized payload envelope

HEAD + BODY + TAIL. Mandatory at every hand-off in a workflow_root skill.

### 3.3.1 Schema home (closes 2-B.1)

`lib/envelope-schema.yaml` — single source of truth. Tests reference it. Documentation generates from it. Schema-version bumps go through meta-infra mode (Chapter 4).

### 3.3.2 Envelope structure

```yaml
---
# HEAD
envelope_version: 1
envelope_id: <uuid>
timestamp: 2026-05-28T14:23:00Z
from:
  type: skill | agent | operator | workflow
  name: build
  context: job-cycle-20260528-1310-a3f
to:
  type: skill | agent | subagent | cold-executor
  name: implementer-subagent
  spawn_fresh: true
workflow:
  root: cycle
  phase: build
  job_id: cycle-20260528-1310-a3f
  step: T3
content_type: task-dispatch | brief | trio | review-request | …
brief_forge:
  evaluators_required: [security, completeness]
  policy_version: 1.2
  override: false
  hydration_sources: [knowhow:azure-networking, lessons:L-014]
---

# BODY (free-form per content_type)

---
# TAIL
produced_by:
  skill: build
  version: 3.5.0
  pack: caip-se
  pack_version: 1.0.0
intended_for:
  receiver: implementer-subagent
  expected_outputs: [src/foo.ts, tests/foo.test.ts]
dependencies:
  produces: [T3.code, T3.tests]
  consumes: [T2.code]
  blocked_until: T2.status == DONE
brief_forge_results:
  - eval: security
    result: pass
    duration_ms: 12
  - eval: completeness
    result: pass
    duration_ms: 8
checksum: sha256:abc...
```

### 3.3.3 Replay UX (closes C2-D4)

`bin/li-envelope-replay <envelope-id>` defaults to `--dry-run` (re-execute in sandbox, surface what would happen + diff against current state). Actual re-execution requires `--apply` flag.

Reason: envelopes capture state at the hand-off moment; the world may have moved on. Dry-run + diff lets the operator decide.

### 3.3.4 Storage

`~/.lintel/jobs/<job-id>/envelopes/` — chronological log per job. HEAD + TAIL fully retained; BODY optionally compressed past N envelopes. Archive policy: same as jobs system (move to `_archive/<date>/` on JOB_END).

## 3.4 FR-C — Generated 1:1 wiki

`bin/li-wiki-gen` reads all frontmatter + manifests + navigation declarations + envelope schemas + pack manifests. Generates `docs/wiki/` structure.

### 3.4.1 Outputs

**Primary:** `docs/wiki/` markdown wiki (developer-facing reference)
- index, by-family, by-layer, by-category catalogs
- envelope-format, brief-forge, navigation reference
- per-pack documentation
- system-map (the new operative map)

**Secondary:** `docs/showcase/lintel-the-harness.html` regenerated from same sources. Closes the wiki-vs-showcase drift gap.

**Tertiary (per side-finding):** CLAUDE.md count strings regenerated from authoritative source. The "74 skills / 44 agents" drift goes away.

### 3.4.2 Generation contract

- Pre-commit hook on structural-path changes (`^(skills|agents|hooks|packs)/.*`) triggers regen
- CI staleness check on every PR (warn-only for v4.0; fail from v4.1)
- Runtime budget: ≤5s typical, ≤15s ceiling
- Idempotent: running twice produces no diff
- Explicit `IGNORE_PATHS:` for handcrafted docs (LAYERS.md, CORE-PRINCIPLES.md, lessons.md, memory.md, ADRs) — wiki includes them by `<include path>` not by replacement

## 3.5 Chapter 2 closing thought

Brief Forge is the layer where v4.0's mechanical guarantee finally shows up. Every hand-off curated, hydrated, evaluated, recorded. Envelope is the artifact. Wiki is the proof.

# §4 Chapter 3 — Engineering depth (5 modules · scaffolding-pattern)

## 4.1 What the operator asked for

Five domains must be exceptional: Technical Architecture, Data Architecture, Security & Compliance, DevOps & Hosting, Testing & QA. Each domain needs granularity from full-process to single-action. Preferences in main profile. Process matters more than current depth: enough hops, gradual context production, checkpoints, failure recovery, continuation-after-fix without breaking, raise-help when needed. Each section has its own quality loop.

## 4.2 Resolving the L-001 concern: modules ship as scaffolding-pattern, not curated content

Review finding S0-P1.3: 35 net-new sub-skills risk being curated content (`ta-api-design`, `da-pii-scan`, etc.) — which would break L-001.

**Resolution preserving full scope:** Each engineering-module sub-skill ships as **workflow + dispatch contract**, NOT as a curated implementation. Per L-001:

- SKILL.md frontmatter is contract (what this skill takes + produces + dispatches to)
- Workflow section is the loop shape (entry → gate → emit → checkpoint → recovery)
- Agent-mapping is the dispatch table
- **Actual recommendations / content are generated by the agent at invocation time**

Example: `ta-api-design/SKILL.md` declares it accepts `--service <name>` + `--scope <breaking|additive>`, dispatches to `APIDesigner` (existing agent) + `BackendArchitect`, produces a versioned interface spec following the dispatch contract. **It does not pre-bake "use REST" or "always version with /v1/" — those are agent decisions at invocation.**

This is exactly how `generate-*` family works today: orchestrator + sub-skills are scaffolding; agent decides content. Engineering modules follow the same pattern.

## 4.3 Resolving the L-002 concern: per-module inventory mandatory

Review finding 1-P1.2: Engineering modules overlap existing families. Verified overlaps:
- `tq-coverage-audit` ↔ `generate-qa`
- `sc-orchestrator` ↔ `compliance-gate` (which IS already an orchestrator)
- `dh-ci-design` ↔ Azure-toolbox skills
- `ta-api-design` ↔ `APIDesigner` agent

**Resolution:** Each module's PR ships with a mandatory L-002 inventory section before the sub-skill list:

```markdown
## L-002 inventory — what exists in this domain

### Existing skills + agents (reuse, don't recreate):
- skills/X/SKILL.md (file:line of contract that overlaps)
- agents/Y/Z.md (agent we will dispatch to, not recreate)

### What this module ADDS:
- Orchestration layer for the existing assets
- N new sub-skills with specific roles below

### What this module REUSES vs OVERLAPS:
- REUSES: <list of existing skills called by this module>
- OVERLAP-RESOLVED: <existing skill X is the canonical for Y; this module dispatches to it>
```

Spine rejects an engineering-module PR that lacks the L-002 inventory.

## 4.4 The module pattern — factored once (resolves 2-P2.1)

```yaml
# THE MODULE TEMPLATE — factored once, referenced by each module
name: <domain>-module
layer: foundation
workflow_root: true
description: <domain> as a callable module — full / loop / single granularity

navigation:
  valid_entries: [full, loop, single]
  valid_exits: [<gate-name>]
  auto_mode_eligible: false
  risk_level: medium
  brief_forge_handoffs:
    on_subagent_spawn:
      enabled: true
      evaluators: [<domain>-eval, security]
    on_phase_transition:
      enabled: true
      evaluators: [completeness]

domain:
  preferences_root: engineering.<domain>.*
  granularities: [full, loop, single]
  checkpoints:
    - <name>: <pass-criterion>
  recovery:
    on_failure: revert-to-last-locked-checkpoint
    after_3_loops: raise_help
  continuation:
    after_fix: resume-at-failed-checkpoint
  raise_help:
    when: <conditions>
    to_whom: operator
  token_budget:
    full: <N>k
    loop: <M>k
    single: <K>k
```

Each module-spec lists ONLY pack-specific deltas: granularities sub-list, sub-skill names, checkpoint criteria, agent additions, hook additions, profile preferences, token-budget numbers. The pattern stays factored.

## 4.5 Module specs — deltas only

For each of the 5 modules, the spec is the DELTAS from the template above.

### 4.5.1 `tech-architecture` (TA)

**L-002 inventory pre-PR:** APIDesigner agent (existing) · Architect agent (existing) · BackendArchitect agent (existing). Module ADDS: orchestration layer + SystemArchitect + CapacityPlanner agents + sub-skills below. REUSES: APIDesigner, Architect, BackendArchitect.

**Granularities:** full / loop / single.

**Sub-skills (scaffolding-pattern; agent generates content at invocation):**
- `ta-api-design` (dispatches to APIDesigner)
- `ta-dependency-graph` (dispatches to Explorer + Architect)

**New hooks (3):** `arch-drift-warn`, `contract-collision-warn`, `complexity-budget-warn`.

2. Decision documented (ADR drafted)
3. Contract locked (interface signed, versioned)
4. Complexity within budget
5. Non-functionals specified

### 4.5.3 `security-compliance` (SC)

**L-002 inventory pre-PR:** 8 security agents + 6 compliance agents + 13 compliance skills + 7 block-hooks ALL EXIST. Module ADDS: SCOrchestrator (the entry) + sc-remediation-plan. REUSES: ALL of the above.

This module is the canonical "orchestrate-don't-recreate" example.

**Sub-skills:** `sc-orchestrator`, `sc-remediation-plan` (only 2 NEW; rest is dispatch).

**L-002 inventory pre-PR:** 7 devops agents + EV2/OneBranch validation + brand-staleness + Azure-toolbox skills EXIST. Module ADDS: SREOrchestrator + sub-skills below. REUSES: 7 existing agents + EV2 validation + Azure-toolbox.

**L-002 inventory pre-PR:** TestRunner (existing) · RegressionDetective (existing) · build-pilot test (existing) · generate-qa skill (existing). Module ADDS: QAOrchestrator + FlakinessHunter + sub-skills below. REUSES: TestRunner, RegressionDetective, generate-qa.

**Sub-skills:** `tq-coverage-audit` (dispatches to generate-qa NOT recreates), `tq-regression-design`, `tq-mutation-test`, `tq-e2e-design`, `tq-contract-test`, `tq-load-test`, `tq-flakiness-hunt`.

**New agents (2):** QAOrchestrator, FlakinessHunter.

**New hooks (3):** `coverage-drop-warn`, `flaky-test-quarantine-warn`, `behavior-test-missing-warn` (closes v3.6 gap 6.9 systemically).

**Checkpoints (NOW WITH RECOVERY + RAISE-HELP per finding 2-P2.1):**
1. Coverage target met per file class (unit ≥80, behavior ≥60, e2e key-path ≥1)
2. Regression suite covers diff-touched code paths
3. No flaky tests in critical path
4. E2E acceptance met for new user-flows
5. Contract tests PASS for changed interfaces

**Recovery:** Revert to last-locked checkpoint. After 3 loops, raise help.
**Continuation:** Resume at failed checkpoint.
**Raise help:** When coverage gap is structural (can't be reached without refactor) → operator decides.

**Token budget:** full 70k, loop 25k, single 8k.

**Profile preferences (`engineering.testing_qa.*`):**

```yaml

    unit_coverage_target: 80
    behavior_coverage_target: 60
    require_regression_on_diff: true
    mutation_test_on_critical: true
    e2e_required_for_user_flows: true
    flakiness_tolerance_pct: 0
    test_runner: pytest
```

## 4.6 Composition — full engineering pass

Composition pattern with declared parallel-eligible boundaries (resolves 1-P2.4 + closes C3-D3):

```
BUILD-phase composition (DAG with parallel-eligible boundaries):

   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │   01 · tech-architecture (TA)  ║  02 · data-architecture (DA)│   ← parallel
   │              ↓ contract+schema locked checkpoint              │
   │   03 · implementation (code emit per plan.md)                 │
   │              ↓ atomic-commit per task                         │
   │   04 · security-compliance (SC) ║ 05 · devops-hosting (DH)   │   ← parallel
   │              ↓ all-checkpoints-green                          │
   │   06 · testing-qa (TQ)                                        │
   │              ↓ coverage-targets-met                           │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ↓
                   REVIEW (cross-domain consistency)
                            ↓
                          SHIP
```

**Token budget for full engineering pass (resolves 4-P1.1):** TA+DA in parallel use max(80k, 75k)=80k. impl uses 50k (plan.md execution). SC+DH in parallel use max(60k, 80k)=80k. TQ uses 70k. **Total module budget: 280k.** Other cycle phases (SENSE, DEFINE, DISCOVER, PLAN, REVIEW, SHIP, CAPTURE): 220k. **Full pass fits in 500k customer-engagement cap.**

When full pass needs more headroom (large engagements), operator can `/li:cycle --mode customer-engagement-deep` — a new 6th mode envelope:

```yaml
customer-engagement-deep:
  cap: 750k soft / 1000k hard
  audience: customer
  voice_tier: trailblazer
  compliance: full_SDL
  use_when: customer-bound deliverable with full engineering depth + complex scope
```

This is the cleanest resolution: new mode for new ambition rather than stretching an existing one.

## 4.7 Single-action entry — "we are not the dumb tool"

Operator's stated value. Implemented via the `single` granularity on every module:

```
/li:ta single --action api-design       → just API design, returns spec
/li:sc single --action threat-model     → just threat model
/li:dh single --action ci-design        → just CI design
/li:tq single --action coverage-audit   → just coverage audit
```

5-15 min each. ~8-10k tokens. Operator picks granularity. Lintel respects it.

## 4.8 Chapter 3 closing thought

Scaffolding-pattern + L-002 inventory per module + factored template means 35 net-new sub-skills can ship without L-001 violation. The full lake, disciplined.

# §5 Chapter 4 — Meta-infra discipline

## 5.1 What the operator asked for

When the WORK is "build infrastructure for Lintel itself" (v3.8 jobs, this v4.0 reframe, future skill-family additions), the process should be different from feature work. Output is structure, not content. Risks differ. Validation differs.

## 5.2 The `meta-infra` mode envelope

Sixth mode joins the five existing envelopes:

```yaml
meta-infra:
  phases: ALL_8 (heavier REVIEW + CAPTURE)
  cap: 600k soft / 900k hard
  audience: operator + future-operator
  voice_tier: internal
  compliance: scaffolding-only (skip customer-facing gates)
  use_when: change touches skills/, agents/, hooks/, bin/_*.sh, install/, LAYERS.md, lib/, packs/, core templates
```

**SENSE auto-detection:** Path-glob matches `^(skills|agents|hooks|bin|lib|packs|install)/.*` in operator's cwd diff. **Recommendation only** — operator confirms per C4-D2.

## 5.3 Audit-override store (resolves 1-P2.2)

`~/.lintel/audit/meta-infra-overrides.jsonl` — append-only log, operator-visible, queryable.

```json
{"ts":"2026-05-29T14:00:00Z","operator":"jokerman","cycle_id":"cycle-...","category":"meta-infra-mode-override","detected_mode":"meta-infra","chosen_mode":"internal-tool","reason":"<operator text>"}
```

After 3 audited overrides in 30 days, SENSE surfaces a prompt: "Your recent structural changes have skipped meta-infra mode (3 in 30 days). Review your override pattern?"

Same store used for orientator auto-mode overrides (Ch.1 §2.5.2). One store, multiple categories. Queryable via `/li:status --audit`.

## 5.4 Meta-infra-specific gates (4 mandatory inside REVIEW)

### Gate M1 — Structure-impact analysis

Before any structural change merges, declare:

```
Affected: skills/X/ + hooks/Y/
Pattern delta: <what changes in the SHAPE, not just the content>
Backward-compat: <which existing usages continue to work as-is>
Migration path: <if break-changes, the migration discipline>
Forward-compat: <what future patterns this enables or forecloses>
```

Stored as `docs/v4.x/structure-changes/<date>-<slug>.md`. CAPTURE auto-creates from cycle context.

### Gate M2 — Compatibility audit (mechanical sweep)

Script that scans 141 skills + 83 agents + 18 hooks asking:

- Does this change affect frontmatter contracts they depend on?
- Does this change rename or move a referenced path?
- Does this change new-default a previously-optional field?
- Does this change a shared helper (`bin/_aliases.sh`, `bin/_jobs.sh`, `lib/pack-resolver.sh`)?

Output: `docs/v4.x/compatibility-audits/<date>-<slug>.md` listing every affected artifact + risk class.

### Gate M3 — Regression shape-tests (resolves 3-P1.2)

**Initial shape-test inventory** (ships in Phase 1, ready for Gate M3 to fire):

| Test | What it asserts | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `frontmatter-lint-all` | Every SKILL.md + agent .md has required frontmatter fields | `tests/shape/frontmatter-lint-all.sh` |
| `agents-categorized` | Every agent in `agents/<category>/` declares matching `category:` | `tests/shape/agents-categorized.sh` |
| `catalog-regenerates-clean` | CATALOG.md regenerates idempotently | `tests/shape/catalog-regenerates-clean.sh` |
| `deprecated-aliases-resolve` | Every deprecated_alias declared in skill frontmatter resolves to a real new-name | `tests/shape/deprecated-aliases-resolve.sh` |
| `workflow-root-has-navigation` | NEW v4.0: every `workflow_root: true` skill declares `navigation:` block | `tests/shape/workflow-root-has-navigation.sh` |
| `brief-forge-handoffs-canonical` | NEW v4.0: only `brief_forge_handoffs:` field name used (no `brief_forge:` alias) | `tests/shape/brief-forge-canonical.sh` |
| `pack-resolver-fallbacks` | The 9-scenario harness from §2.2 | `tests/shape/pack-resolver-fallbacks.sh` |
| `schema-versioned-contracts` | Every contract JSON in `lib/` declares `schema_version` | `tests/shape/schema-versioned-contracts.sh` |

Shape-tests live in `tests/shape/`. Documented in `tests/shape/_README.md`. Test runner picks them up automatically.

When a shape-test fails inside meta-infra REVIEW, the cycle BLOCKS. No bypass without explicit override + audit.

### Gate M4 — Future-operator validation

Operator + Claude walk a fresh-cold-session scenario: "Six months from now, an operator (could be you) opens this for the first time. Read only the README + LAYERS.md + the affected concept doc. Can they understand what changed and why?"

If no → CAPTURE must produce a concept doc + a migration note. If yes → proceed.

## 5.5 Output contract: change-log + migration-guide as one document

Standard cycle CAPTURE produces lessons.md + ADR + memory.md updates. Meta-infra CAPTURE produces all of those PLUS a `MIGRATION.md` entry under `docs/v4.x/migrations/<date>-<slug>.md`:

```markdown
# Migration: <date> — <change summary>

## What changed (shape)
<the structural delta from Gate M1>

## What still works without action
<list of unchanged callsites>

## What requires migration
<callsite> → <new-shape> (estimated effort: <S/M/L>)

## Compatibility window
- Grace period: <until-when>
- Removal date: <when the old shape is removed>
- Tracker: docs/v4.x/migrations/_INDEX.md entry <name>

## Test discipline
- Shape-tests added: <which>
- Regression coverage: <statement>

## Rollback procedure
<if this migration goes wrong, here's how>
```

**Tracker store (resolves 2-P3.3):** `docs/v4.x/migrations/_INDEX.md` is the durable tracker. Each migration MD file is the unit of work. `tasks/memory.md` does NOT track migration windows — it stays ephemeral working memory.

## 5.6 The `/li:migrations` skill (NEW v4.0)

Sister to `/li:status`. Surfaces pending migrations at SENSE.

Reads `docs/v4.x/migrations/_INDEX.md` + per-file frontmatter. For each active migration with operator-callsites still on old shape:

```
⚠ Migration <slug> — grace until <date> (<N> days remaining)
   Old callsites detected in: <files>
   Action: <one-line>
```

Read-only. Doesn't migrate code automatically. Surfaces the work; operator decides.

## 5.7 When meta-infra applies vs not — the discipline table

| Work type | Mode | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Build a new feature in a customer engagement | customer-engagement | content work, not infrastructure |
| Fix a bug in an existing skill | hotfix | targeted fix, no structural change |
| Add a new skill to an existing family | internal-tool | additive, no contract change |
| Add a new agent category (like v3.7 frontend/) | **meta-infra** | new structural pattern |
| Change frontmatter contract | **meta-infra** | affects every skill/agent |
| Move a `bin/` helper | **meta-infra** | affects every caller |
| Rename a skill (per alias-mekanism) | **meta-infra** | affects callsites + plugin manifests |
| Add a new mode envelope | **meta-infra** | affects cycle behavior |
| Add a new layer to LAYERS.md | **meta-infra** | foundational change |
| Add a pack-bound concept to PackResolver | **meta-infra** | affects ~30+ skills |
| Modify Brief Forge evaluator registry | **meta-infra** | affects every hand-off |

When in doubt, SENSE recommends meta-infra. Operator can downgrade after Gate M1 if impact analysis confirms a smaller surface.

## 5.8 Meta-application: this v4.0 reframe IS a meta-infra cycle

Closing the loop: the v4.0 reframe is harness-on-harness work. We dogfood meta-infra immediately:

- Gate M1 (structure-impact): this doc IS the impact analysis
- Gate M2 (compatibility-audit): pack-resolver test harness (Ch.1 §2.2 A.7) + cross-skill `grep -r` sweep
- Gate M3 (regression shape-tests): the 8 shape-tests above
- Gate M4 (future-operator validation): operator review of this doc IS the validation

Shipping v4.0 IS the first meta-infra cycle execution.

## 5.9 Chapter 4 closing thought

Meta-infra mode is the gate that protects the gate-builder. Self-modifying systems need self-aware processes. The discipline applies to itself: the reframe ships under the reframe's own rules.

# §6 Chapter 5 — Composition · ship sequencing · phases

## 6.1 Cross-chapter dependency graph

```
Chapter 4 (meta-infra mode) → governs how subsequent chapters ship
       ↓
Chapter 1.A (spine extraction)
       ↓
Chapter 1.B (pack architecture) — pack.yaml includes brief_forge_handoffs: block
       ↓                              ↑
Chapter 1.D (CAIP-SE lift)          Chapter 2.B (envelope schema, small, ships anytime)
       ↓                              ↑
Chapter 1.C (navigation)            Chapter 2.A (Brief Forge depends on envelope + pack)
       ↓                              ↑
                                    Chapter 2.C (wiki gen depends on all above)
       ↓                              ↑
       └──→ Chapter 3 — Engineering depth ←──┘
            5 modules ship sequentially per C3-D1 ordering
```

## 6.2 Ship phases — five phases for full v4.0

**Phase 1 — v4.0-alpha (~5-7 CC-days):** meta-infra mode + spine extraction + initial shape-tests

- Ship meta-infra mode FIRST. We need it to govern Phase 1+ which IS structural.
- Then Chapter 1.A spine extraction under meta-infra discipline (proof-of-process).
- Ship the 8 initial shape-tests so Gate M3 can fire.
- Output: spine works pack-neutral; meta-infra mode active; shape-tests live.

**Phase 2 — v4.0-beta (~5-7 CC-days):** pack architecture + CAIP-SE lift + envelope schema

- Chapter 1.B pack architecture under meta-infra.
- Chapter 1.D CAIP-SE pack under standard internal-tool (content-migration).
- Chapter 2.B envelope schema under meta-infra (small but structural).
- `/li:v4-migrate` skill ships here (R1 mitigation: automate the operator's caip-se switch).
- Output: packs work; operator's daily workflow continues via caip-se pack; envelope schema exists.

**Phase 3 — v4.0-rc (~6-8 CC-days):** navigation + Brief Forge + wiki gen

- Chapter 1.C navigation under meta-infra.
- Chapter 2.A Brief Forge under meta-infra (large structural addition).
- Chapter 2.C wiki gen under standard internal-tool (reads sources, doesn't change them).
- `/li:forge-stats` skill (R2 mitigation: latency telemetry from day one).
- Output: every workflow_root has navigation; every hand-off goes through Brief Forge; wiki + showcase + CLAUDE.md counts auto-regenerate.

**Phase 4 — v4.0 ship + engineering depth start (~9-12 CC-days for first 2 modules)**

- v4.0 ship gate validation (operator validation criteria, §9 pass).
- Tag `v4.0.0-dev`.
- Engineering modules start. **First two modules ship in this phase per C3-D1 — recommend TA + SC (TA proves the pattern; SC proves the orchestrate-don't-recreate discipline).**

**Phase 5 — engineering depth completion (~12-18 CC-days for remaining 3 modules)**

- DA, DH, TQ modules ship in operator-chosen order.
- Each module's PR ships with mandatory L-002 inventory (per §4.3).
- Each module shipped under standard internal-tool (additive feature work).
- Tag `v4.5.0-dev` when all 5 modules complete.

**Total estimate: ~37-52 CC-days for full v4.x rollout.**

| Phase | Scope | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| 1 alpha | meta-infra + spine extraction + shape-tests | 5-7 days |
| 2 beta | packs + CAIP-SE + envelope schema | 5-7 days |
| 3 rc | navigation + Brief Forge + wiki | 6-8 days |
| 4 ship | validation + first 2 engineering modules | 9-12 days |
| 5 complete | remaining 3 engineering modules | 12-18 days |
| **TOTAL** | | **37-52 days** |

## 6.3 Cross-cutting risks (5)

- **R1 — v4.0 reframe is fundamental contract change.** Existing CAIP-SE users must switch to caip-se pack. **Mitigation:** `/li:v4-migrate` skill (Phase 2) walks operator through swap.
- **R2 — Brief Forge latency <1s needs telemetry from day one.** Unfalsifiable without measurement. **Mitigation:** envelope TAIL records duration_ms per evaluator. `/li:forge-stats` skill in Phase 3.
- **R3 — Engineering modules risk over-specification.** Ambitious spec may force scope reduction. **Mitigation:** Phase 4 ships ONLY TA + SC. Validate pattern. Decide on remaining 3 modules' scope per real friction.
- **R4 — Meta-infra friction; operator may resent on small refactors.** **Mitigation:** SENSE auto-detection generous (only triggers on contract-affecting patterns). Small additive changes (new skill in existing family) stay in internal-tool.
- **R5 — Wiki generation obscures handcrafted docs.** **Mitigation:** Explicit `IGNORE_PATHS:` for LAYERS.md, CORE-PRINCIPLES.md, lessons.md, memory.md, ADRs. Wiki includes by `<include path>` not replacement.

## 6.4 Chapter 5 closing thought

Five phases, two tags (`v4.0.0-dev` after Phase 4, `v4.5.0-dev` after Phase 5), 37-52 CC-days. The full lake, disciplined into shippable units.

  - **Recommendation: TA + SC together in Phase 4.** TA proves the scaffolding-pattern; SC proves the orchestrate-don't-recreate discipline. Pair sets the bar for the remaining 3.
  - Alternative: ship TA alone in Phase 4; defer SC to Phase 5.

That's the entire list. Everything else in §7 is a recommendation with a default.

# §9 Operator validation criteria (10 mechanical pass/fail tests)

Replaces v1's mostly-mechanical criteria; #10 reformulated per finding 3-P1.1.

1. **Pack neutrality:** `grep -r "Trailblazer\|CAIP-SE\|RAIS\|OneCS" skills/ agents/ hooks/` returns no execution-path matches.
2. **Pack swap behavior:** `/li:pack-switch caip-se` produces today's behavior. `/li:pack-switch _default` produces neutral behavior. No code changes.
3. **Navigation guarantee:** A `workflow_root: true` skill without `navigation:` block is rejected at load. `tests/shape/workflow-root-has-navigation.sh` PASS.
4. **Brief Forge coverage:** Every hand-off in cycle/plan/build/ship/capture runs through Brief Forge. Override-with-audit works. `tests/shape/brief-forge-canonical.sh` PASS.
5. **Brief Forge performance:** p95 wall-clock latency over 100 invocations < 1000ms via `lib/brief-forge/bench.sh`.
6. **Envelope adoption:** Every hand-off produces an envelope. `/li:envelope-replay <id> --dry-run` works end-to-end on a fixture envelope.
7. **Wiki accuracy:** `bin/li-wiki-gen` regenerates idempotently (re-run = no diff). Includes CLAUDE.md count-strings.
8. **Engineering depth:** Each of the 5 modules can be invoked standalone (`/li:ta single --action api-design` etc.) and complete its loop with checkpoint verdict. **At v4.0 ship-gate (end of Phase 4), this passes for TA + SC. Full criterion holds at end of Phase 5.**
9. **Meta-infra discipline:** Any change to `skills/` / `agents/` / `hooks/` / `bin/` / `lib/` / `packs/` / `install/` defaults to meta-infra mode. Gate M2 runs automatically.
10. **Mechanical pack-new validation (replaces v1's 6-months-later test):** `/li:pack-new --interactive --dry-run` produces a valid pack.yaml that passes the pack-validation hook in ≤10 prompts. Verifies fresh-operator UX without requiring a fresh operator.

Re-stated for clarity. Mitigations encoded in chapter sections noted.

| R3 — Engineering modules over-specification | Ship 2 modules in Phase 4 first, validate, then decide on remaining 3 | §6.2 Phase 4-5 |

# Appendix C — Operator stance carried through

Operator told me to honor intent. The stances carried through every chapter:

- **Bold + effective + operator carries responsibility.** Every gate ships with override + audit. No paternalism.
- **Refusal of padding for novice protection.** No hand-holding. Pack interview asks essentials in condensed form.
- **Opinionated about what spine demands from any workflow.** Navigation and `brief_forge_handoffs:` are mandatory, not optional.
- **Sequential where it pays, parallel where it helps.** Engineering modules compose with declared parallel-eligible boundaries (DAG).
- **Mechanical first, LLM on escalation.** Brief Forge evaluators, orientator routing, all default to mechanical parsing with budgeted LLM fallback.
- **Defense through transparency, not blocking.** Override-with-audit is the pattern. Trust the operator.
- **Compounding edge through discipline, not toolchain.** Pack vault, envelope log, generated wiki — all compound over time.
- **Portability from day one** (added in v2.0). Multi-CLI + pack-swap + schema-version + audit-JSONL — all four dimensions woven through every chapter.
